change.reason: B states the separate cohorts, before/after pairing, X/Z rate-first equal weighting, separate 40-set random mean, correct distinct improvement denominators, and independent 5,000 test shots per hardware setting. F expresses the same facts in a compressed form: its .130% “original gap” is .215−.130, and its 50,000×10% test budget is read per duration/patch/basis from the stated paper setup. A has correct two improvements and mechanisms but omits cohort pairing, aggregation, and sample budget (0.5). D has correct cohorts, test budget, and mechanisms but omits aggregation and quantitative improvement denominators (0.5). C falsely labels 10,000 as independent test shots; 10,000 is validation plus test. E pools unequal X/Z denominators contrary to (B1). Both incorrect assertions receive 0.
issues: F does not repeat “per duration, patch, basis” explicitly. It earns full credit only when its 50,000→5,000 statement is read under the question’s per-setting context; B is the unambiguous preferred answer.
The 8×10^9 baseline used for attribution and 5.7402×10^9 per before/after intervention case are different simulation batches; they must not be numerically paired.
